chapters.title: Chapter 1: Federal Appellate Jurisdiction and Standards of Review
chapters.description: Explains when federal courts of appeals may review district court decisions and how they evaluate summary judgment rulings.
subtopics: Final judgment rule and appealability
De novo review of summary judgment
Genuine dispute of material fact under Rule 56
Viewing the record in the light most favorable to the nonmovant
Effect of stipulations on appellate review

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Article III Justiciability—Standing, Mootness, and Voluntary Cessation
chapters.description: Provides the constitutional prerequisites for federal jurisdiction and how they apply when defendants alter challenged conduct during litigation.
subtopics: Injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability
Mootness doctrine and the need for a live controversy
Voluntary cessation and the 'absolutely clear' standard
Prospective relief and likelihood of recurrence
Redressability where relief takes the form of civil penalties

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Landmark Doctrine—Laidlaw, Mesquite, and Concentrated Phosphate
chapters.description: Synthesizes the Supreme Court’s voluntary cessation and mootness framework and its application to civil penalties and ongoing violations.
subtopics: Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw: civil penalties payable to the government as redress and deterrence
City of Mesquite v. Aladdin’s Castle: effect of voluntary cessation on mootness
United States v. Concentrated Phosphate Export Ass’n: 'absolutely clear' standard
Applying these principles to compliance changes and policy withdrawals

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Landmark Doctrine—Town of Chester and Relief-Specific Standing
chapters.description: Explains the requirement that a plaintiff must have standing for each claim and each specific form of relief requested.
subtopics: Claim-specific and remedy-specific standing
Implications for suits seeking damages, penalties, and injunctive relief
Interplay with class or representative allegations
Jurisdictional inquiries at different stages of litigation

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Overview of Minnesota Wage-and-Hour Framework
chapters.description: Introduces Minnesota’s principal wage statutes and how they interrelate with enforcement by the state and private litigants.
subtopics: Minnesota Payment of Wages Act (MPWA): timing and payment of wages
Minnesota Fair Labor Standards Act (MFLSA): minimum wage and overtime
Minnesota Wage Theft Act (MWTA): notice, recordkeeping, and protections
Role of the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry and the Commissioner
Private civil actions versus administrative enforcement

chapters.title: Chapter 6: MPWA—Wage Payment, Enforcement, and Remedies
chapters.description: Details the MPWA’s core obligations, private enforcement provision, and the allocation of penalties and other relief.
subtopics: Timely payment of wages and commissions
Private right of action under Minn. Stat. § 181.171
Commissioner’s authority to demand payment and assess penalties under § 181.101
Availability of compensatory damages and 'other appropriate relief' in private suits
Comparison with §§ 181.13 and 181.14 (discharge/resignation penalties upon demand)
Limitations on employee recovery of statutory penalties

chapters.title: Chapter 7: MFLSA—Overtime, Liquidated Damages, and Civil Penalties
chapters.description: Covers Minnesota’s overtime requirements and the remedial scheme, including who may recover which remedies and how they are enforced.
subtopics: Overtime requirements and exemptions (Minn. Stat. § 177.25)
Enforcement authority and remedies (Minn. Stat. § 177.27)
Liquidated damages versus civil penalties
Collection and allocation of civil penalties
Interaction between private actions and the Commissioner’s remedies

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Landmark Doctrine—Milner v. Farmers Insurance Exchange
chapters.description: Explores Minnesota Supreme Court precedent interpreting MFLSA remedies and the relationship between private suits and Commissioner-enforced penalties.
subtopics: Scope of private enforcement of MFLSA remedies
Who receives civil penalties and how they are collected
Availability of injunctive relief in wage-and-hour cases under Minnesota law
Interpreting remedial statutes in harmony with administrative enforcement

chapters.title: Chapter 9: MWTA—Notice, Recordkeeping, and Enforcement
chapters.description: Explains employer obligations to provide written notice of terms and changes to pay practices and the enforcement architecture for violations.
subtopics: Required written notices, including pay rate and overtime policies (Minn. Stat. § 181.032)
Recordkeeping duties and timing of notice for policy changes
Available remedies and who may seek them
Overlap with MPWA and MFLSA claims
Limits on private recovery of penalties under the MWTA

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Remedies in Wage-and-Hour Litigation
chapters.description: Surveys monetary and equitable remedies commonly sought in wage cases and the statutory and equitable constraints on their availability.
subtopics: Back wages, overtime premiums, and restitution
Liquidated damages: purposes and calculation
Civil penalties: purpose, payee, and deterrence
Prejudgment interest and attorneys’ fees under fee-shifting provisions
Standards and prerequisites for injunctive relief

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Minnesota Statutory Interpretation
chapters.description: Provides canons and methods Minnesota courts use to interpret statutes, with emphasis on remedial and penalty provisions.
subtopics: Plain meaning and unambiguous text
Context, structure, and cross-reference analysis
Expressio unius and the 'knows how to' canon
Harmonizing overlapping statutes
Use of administrative enforcement provisions to infer private remedies

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Erie and State-Law Claims in Federal Court
chapters.description: Explains how federal courts adjudicate state-law claims, including reliance on state supreme court precedent and prediction of state law.
subtopics: Erie doctrine and the distinction between substantive state law and federal procedure
Hierarchy of state-court authority (supreme court, intermediate courts)
Use of federal district court decisions as persuasive authority
Certification to state supreme courts (when available)
Applying state remedial schemes in federal actions

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Civil Procedure—Issue Preservation, Waiver, and Appellate Briefing
chapters.description: Covers how parties preserve arguments for appeal and the consequences of raising new theories late in litigation.
subtopics: Preserving arguments at summary judgment
Raising new claims through amended pleadings versus briefing
Federal Rule of Appellate Procedure 28(a)(9)(A) requirements
Waiver and forfeiture doctrines on appeal
Standards for considering inadequately briefed issues

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Amending Pleadings and Seeking Injunctive Relief
chapters.description: Describes procedural mechanisms for modifying claims and obtaining equitable relief in federal court.
subtopics: Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(a) and standards for amendment
Pleading versus proof for injunctive relief
Specificity and scope of requested injunctions
Changing requested remedies during litigation
Effects on appellate review when relief sought changes

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Stipulations, Offers of Relief, and Justiciability
chapters.description: Analyzes how payments or stipulations concerning damages interact with standing and mootness for remaining forms of relief.
subtopics: Stipulated payments and remaining live controversies
Partial resolution and the continuing case-or-controversy requirement
Impact on claims for penalties and injunctive relief
Court authority to vacate and remand for jurisdictional determinations

chapters.title: Chapter 16: The Role of Precedent and Use of Authority
chapters.description: Explains how courts apply precedent to interpret statutes and resolve procedural questions, including the interplay between federal and state authority.
subtopics: Binding versus persuasive authority
Applying Supreme Court justiciability doctrine in lower federal courts
Relying on state supreme court interpretations for state statutes
Reading remedial provisions in light of prior case law
